passages.text: After these events, King Xerxes honored Haman son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, elevating him to a position above all the princes who were with him.
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes was the ruler of Persia.
Haman was the son of Hammedatha.
Haman was an Agagite.
After these events, King Xerxes honored Haman.
King Xerxes promoted Haman.
King Xerxes gave Haman a high position.
King Xerxes placed Haman’s seat above all the other princes who served with him.
passages.original: אַחַ֣ר׀ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֗לֶּה גִּדַּל֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵר֜וֹשׁ אֶת־ הָמָ֧ן בֶּֽן־ הַמְּדָ֛תָא הָאֲגָגִ֖י וַֽיְנַשְּׂאֵ֑הוּ וַיָּ֙שֶׂם֙ אֶת־ כִּסְא֔וֹ מֵעַ֕ל כָּל־ הַשָּׂרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: All the royal servants at the king’s gate bowed down and paid homage to Haman, because the king had commanded that this be done for him. But Mordecai would not bow down or pay homage.
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes ruled the land.
He commanded all his royal servants at the king’s gate to honor Haman.
Haman was the son of Hammedatha.
Haman was an Agagite.
The king ordered everyone to bow down to Haman.
The royal servants obeyed the king.
They bowed down to Haman.
They paid homage to Haman.
Mordecai was also at the king’s gate.
Mordecai was a Jew.
Mordecai did not bow down to Haman.
Mordecai did not pay homage to Haman.
passages.original: וְכָל־ עַבְדֵ֨י הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֲשֶׁר־ בְּשַׁ֣עַר הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ כֹּרְעִ֤ים וּמִֽשְׁתַּחֲוִים֙ לְהָמָ֔ן כִּי־ כֵ֖ן צִוָּה־ ל֣וֹ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וּמָ֨רְדֳּכַ֔י לֹ֥א יִכְרַ֖ע וְלֹ֥א יִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֶֽה׃

passages.text: Then the royal servants at the king’s gate asked Mordecai, “Why do you disobey the command of the king?”
passages.sermon:
Mordecai was a Jew.
He worked at the king’s gate.
King Xerxes had commanded everyone to honor Haman.
The royal servants at the king’s gate saw Mordecai.
They saw that Mordecai did not obey the king’s command.
The royal servants spoke to Mordecai.
They asked Mordecai a question.
They said, “Why do you disobey the king’s command?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמְר֜וּ עַבְדֵ֥י הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ אֲשֶׁר־ בְּשַׁ֥עַר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לְמָרְדֳּכָ֑י מַדּ֙וּעַ֙ אַתָּ֣ה עוֹבֵ֔ר אֵ֖ת מִצְוַ֥ת הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: Day after day they warned him, but he would not comply. So they reported it to Haman to see whether Mordecai’s behavior would be tolerated, since he had told them he was a Jew.
passages.sermon:
Mordecai was a Jew.
The royal servants stood at the king’s gate.
They spoke to Mordecai every day.
They warned him to obey the king’s command.
Mordecai did not listen to them.
He did not obey their warning.
The servants told Haman about Mordecai.
They wanted to see if Mordecai’s actions would be allowed.
Mordecai had told them he was a Jew.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י בְּאָמְרָם אֵלָיו֙ י֣וֹם וָי֔וֹם וְלֹ֥א שָׁמַ֖ע אֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וַיַּגִּ֣ידוּ לְהָמָ֗ן לִרְאוֹת֙ הֲיַֽעַמְדוּ֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י מָרְדֳּכַ֔י כִּֽי־ הִגִּ֥יד לָהֶ֖ם אֲשֶׁר־ ה֥וּא יְהוּדִֽי׃

passages.text: When Haman saw that Mordecai would not bow down or pay him homage, he was filled with rage.
passages.sermon:
Haman was a high official in King Xerxes’ court.
Haman saw Mordecai at the king’s gate.
Mordecai did not bow down to Haman.
Mordecai did not pay Haman homage.
Haman became very angry.
passages.original: וַיַּ֣רְא הָמָ֔ן כִּי־ אֵ֣ין מָרְדֳּכַ֔י כֹּרֵ֥עַ וּמִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֖ה ל֑וֹ וַיִּמָּלֵ֥א הָמָ֖ן חֵמָֽה׃

passages.text: And when he learned the identity of Mordecai’s people, he scorned the notion of laying hands on Mordecai alone. Instead, he sought to destroy all of Mordecai’s people, the Jews, throughout the kingdom of Xerxes.
passages.sermon:
Haman was a high official in the kingdom of King Xerxes.
Haman learned that Mordecai was a Jew.
Haman knew that Mordecai belonged to the Jewish people.
Haman did not want to harm only Mordecai.
Haman decided not to attack Mordecai alone.
Haman wanted to destroy all the Jews.
Haman planned to destroy all of Mordecai’s people.
Haman wanted to destroy every Jew in the entire kingdom of Xerxes.
passages.original: וַיִּ֣בֶז בְּעֵינָ֗יו לִשְׁלֹ֤ח יָד֙ בְּמָרְדֳּכַ֣י לְבַדּ֔וֹ כִּֽי־ הִגִּ֥ידוּ ל֖וֹ אֶת־ עַ֣ם מָרְדֳּכָ֑י וַיְבַקֵּ֣שׁ הָמָ֗ן לְהַשְׁמִ֧יד אֶת־ כָּל־ הַיְּהוּדִ֛ים אֲשֶׁ֛ר בְּכָל־ מַלְכ֥וּת אֲחַשְׁוֵר֖וֹשׁ עַ֥ם מָרְדֳּכָֽי׃

passages.text: In the twelfth year of King Xerxes, in the first month, the month of Nisan, the Pur (that is, the lot) was cast before Haman to determine a day and month. And the lot fell on the twelfth month, the month of Adar.
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes ruled a vast kingdom.
This event happened in the twelfth year of his reign.
The first month of the year is called Nisan.
Haman was an official in the king’s court.
People cast lots before Haman.
They used lots to choose a day and a month.
The lot is called Pur.
The lot showed a result.
The chosen time was the twelfth month.
The twelfth month is called Adar.
passages.original: בַּחֹ֤דֶשׁ הָרִאשׁוֹן֙ הוּא־ חֹ֣דֶשׁ נִיסָ֔ן בִּשְׁנַת֙ שְׁתֵּ֣ים עֶשְׂרֵ֔ה לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵר֑וֹשׁ הִפִּ֣יל פּוּר֩ ה֨וּא הַגּוֹרָ֜ל לִפְנֵ֣י הָמָ֗ן מִיּ֧וֹם׀ לְי֛וֹם וּמֵחֹ֛דֶשׁ לְחֹ֥דֶשׁ שְׁנֵים־ עָשָׂ֖ר הוּא־ חֹ֥דֶשׁ אֲדָֽר׃ס

passages.text: Then Haman informed King Xerxes, “There is a certain people scattered and dispersed among the peoples of every province of your kingdom. Their laws are different from everyone else’s, and they do not obey the king’s laws. So it is not in the king’s best interest to tolerate them.
passages.sermon:
Haman spoke to King Xerxes.
Haman said, “There is a certain people in your kingdom.
This people lives in every province.
They are scattered among all the other peoples.
Their laws are different from the laws of everyone else.
They do not obey the king’s laws.
It is not good for the king to let them remain.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הָמָן֙ לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵר֔וֹשׁ יֶשְׁנ֣וֹ עַם־ אֶחָ֗ד מְפֻזָּ֤ר וּמְפֹרָד֙ בֵּ֣ין הָֽעַמִּ֔ים בְּכֹ֖ל מְדִינ֣וֹת מַלְכוּתֶ֑ךָ וְדָתֵיהֶ֞ם שֹׁנ֣וֹת מִכָּל־ עָ֗ם וְאֶת־ דָּתֵ֤י הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ אֵינָ֣ם עֹשִׂ֔ים וְלַמֶּ֥לֶךְ אֵין־ שֹׁוֶ֖ה לְהַנִּיחָֽם׃

passages.text: If it pleases the king, let a decree be issued to destroy them, and I will deposit ten thousand talents of silver into the royal treasury to pay those who carry it out.”
passages.sermon:
Haman spoke to King Xerxes.
Haman wanted to destroy a certain people.
Haman said, “If it pleases the king, let a decree be written to destroy them.”
Haman promised to pay ten thousand talents of silver.
Haman would give this money to those who would do the work.
Haman said the silver would go into the king’s treasury.
passages.original: אִם־ עַל־ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ ט֔וֹב יִכָּתֵ֖ב לְאַבְּדָ֑ם וַעֲשֶׂ֨רֶת אֲלָפִ֜ים כִּכַּר־ כֶּ֗סֶף אֶשְׁקוֹל֙ עַל־ יְדֵי֙ עֹשֵׂ֣י הַמְּלָאכָ֔ה לְהָבִ֖יא אֶל־ גִּנְזֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: So the king removed the signet ring from his finger and gave it to Haman son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, the enemy of the Jews.
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes ruled a vast kingdom.
Haman was the son of Hammedatha.
Haman was an Agagite.
Haman was the enemy of the Jews.
King Xerxes took his signet ring off his finger.
King Xerxes gave the signet ring to Haman.
passages.original: וַיָּ֧סַר הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ אֶת־ טַבַּעְתּ֖וֹ מֵעַ֣ל יָד֑וֹ וַֽיִּתְּנָ֗הּ לְהָמָ֧ן בֶּֽן־ הַמְּדָ֛תָא הָאֲגָגִ֖י צֹרֵ֥ר הַיְּהוּדִֽים׃

passages.text: “Keep your money,” said the king to Haman. “These people are given to you to do with them as you please.”
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes spoke to Haman.
King Xerxes was the ruler of the Persian Empire.
Haman was the enemy of the Jews.
King Xerxes said, “You may keep your money.”
King Xerxes said, “I give you these people.”
King Xerxes said, “Do with them as you think is best.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ לְהָמָ֔ן הַכֶּ֖סֶף נָת֣וּן לָ֑ךְ וְהָעָ֕ם לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת בּ֖וֹ כַּטּ֥וֹב בְּעֵינֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: On the thirteenth day of the first month, the royal scribes were summoned and the order was written exactly as Haman commanded the royal satraps, the governors of each province, and the officials of each people, in the script of each province and the language of every people. It was written in the name of King Xerxes and sealed with the royal signet ring.
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes ruled the Persian Empire.
Haman was the enemy of the Jews.
On the thirteenth day of the first month, King Xerxes summoned the royal scribes.
The scribes wrote an order.
They wrote everything exactly as Haman commanded.
They addressed the order to the king’s satraps.
They addressed it to the governors of each province.
They addressed it to the officials of each people.
They wrote the order in the script of each province.
They wrote it in the language of every people.
They wrote the order in the name of King Xerxes.
They sealed it with the king’s signet ring.
passages.original: וַיִּקָּרְאוּ֩ סֹפְרֵ֨י הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָרִאשׁ֗וֹן בִּשְׁלוֹשָׁ֨ה עָשָׂ֣ר יוֹם֮ בּוֹ֒ וַיִּכָּתֵ֣ב כְּֽכָל־ אֲשֶׁר־ צִוָּ֣ה הָמָ֡ן אֶ֣ל אֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנֵֽי־ הַ֠מֶּלֶךְ וְֽאֶל־ הַפַּח֞וֹת אֲשֶׁ֣ר׀ עַל־ מְדִינָ֣ה וּמְדִינָ֗ה וְאֶל־ שָׂ֤רֵי עַם֙ וָעָ֔ם מְדִינָ֤ה וּמְדִינָה֙ כִּכְתָבָ֔הּ וְעַ֥ם וָעָ֖ם כִּלְשׁוֹנ֑וֹ בְּשֵׁ֨ם הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרֹשׁ֙ נִכְתָּ֔ב וְנֶחְתָּ֖ם בְּטַבַּ֥עַת הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: And the letters were sent by couriers to each of the royal provinces with the order to destroy, kill, and annihilate all the Jews—young and old, women and children—and to plunder their possessions on a single day, the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month.
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes ruled over many provinces.
Haman received authority from King Xerxes to act against the Jews.
The king’s scribes wrote letters as Haman commanded.
Couriers carried these letters to every province in the kingdom.
The letters gave a command.
The command was to destroy all the Jews.
This included young people and old people.
This included children and women.
The command was to do this on one day.
That day was the thirteenth day of the twelfth month.
The twelfth month is called Adar.
The command also allowed people to take the possessions of the Jews.
passages.original: וְנִשְׁל֨וֹחַ סְפָרִ֜ים בְּיַ֣ד הָרָצִים֮ אֶל־ כָּל־ מְדִינ֣וֹת הַמֶּלֶךְ֒ לְהַשְׁמִ֡יד לַהֲרֹ֣ג וּלְאַבֵּ֣ד אֶת־ כָּל־ הַ֠יְּהוּדִים מִנַּ֨עַר וְעַד־ זָקֵ֜ן טַ֤ף וְנָשִׁים֙ בְּי֣וֹם אֶחָ֔ד בִּשְׁלוֹשָׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֛ר לְחֹ֥דֶשׁ שְׁנֵים־ עָשָׂ֖ר הוּא־ חֹ֣דֶשׁ אֲדָ֑ר וּשְׁלָלָ֖ם לָבֽוֹז׃

passages.text: A copy of the text of the edict was to be issued in every province and published to all the people, so that they would be ready on that day.
passages.sermon:
A copy of the king’s edict was prepared.
Officials made this copy for every province.
They published the edict in each province.
They made the edict clear to all the people.
Everyone could read and understand the order.
The people needed to be ready for the appointed day.
passages.original: פַּתְשֶׁ֣גֶן הַכְּתָ֗ב לְהִנָּ֤תֵֽן דָּת֙ בְּכָל־ מְדִינָ֣ה וּמְדִינָ֔ה גָּל֖וּי לְכָל־ הָֽעַמִּ֑ים לִהְי֥וֹת עֲתִדִ֖ים לַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: The couriers left, spurred on by the king’s command, and the edict was issued in the citadel of Susa. Then the king and Haman sat down to drink, but the city of Susa was in confusion.
passages.sermon:
The king gave a command.
Couriers hurried out with the king’s command.
Officials issued the edict in the citadel of Susa.
The king and Haman sat down to drink.
The city of Susa was confused.
passages.original: הָֽרָצִ֞ים יָצְא֤וּ דְחוּפִים֙ בִּדְבַ֣ר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְהַדָּ֥ת נִתְּנָ֖ה בְּשׁוּשַׁ֣ן הַבִּירָ֑ה וְהַמֶּ֤לֶךְ וְהָמָן֙ יָשְׁב֣וּ לִשְׁתּ֔וֹת וְהָעִ֥יר שׁוּשָׁ֖ן נָבֽוֹכָה׃פ
